Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
Vanguard Renewables is committed to maintaining high environmental standards in all operations. Activities conducted at this facility have the potential to affect both employees and the surrounding community. As such, Vanguard Renewables prioritizes environmental stewardship, employee health and safety, compliance with applicable regulations, and the prevention of pollution through collaboration and continuous improvement.

The environmental, health, and safety (EHS) procedures at Vanguard Renewables are designed to support the overall safety of this facility, its personnel, and the surrounding public. These guidelines incorporate risk mitigation reduction measures that control operational hazards and prevent incidents impacting health, safety, or the environment. Vanguard Renewables is committed to complying with the OSHA Process Safety Management (PSM) Standard, Title 29 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 1910.119, and EPA Risk Management Program (RMP) regulations, Title 40 CFR Part 68, to address the risks involved with the storage, handling, and processing of methane. This program enables the facility to prevent the occurrence, or minimize the consequences of, significant releases of methane.

It is Vanguard Renewables' policy to conduct operations in accordance with all applicable laws, regulations, and permits and to encourage a safe workplace environment. Each employee is trained and required to comply strictly with this policy.

Stationary Source and Regulated Substance
The Vanguard Renewables Peterson Biogas Facility located at W10322 State Road 29, River Falls, Wisconsin 54022, conducts a biogas production process that generates methane (74-82-8). The facility is classified as Prevention Program 3 and is regulated by EPA RMP and OSHA PSM for the flammable substance methane which is held on site in excess of 10,000 lbs. Though the methane calculated to be on-site is below the 10,000-pound threshol

d, the mixture rule applies as the methane is more than 1 percent of the mixture and, therefore, the entire weight of the mixture was considered (USEPA 2024).

General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical Specific Prevention
The facility demonstrates its commitment to chemical safety is demonstrated through its established management, training, operating procedures, and maintenance systems in place at the facility, and the specific measures in place for the process hazard assessment, prevention program, and emergency action protocols required under the RMP. To manage the biogas process, the facility has implemented the Program 3 Prevention Program guidelines, which are designed to reduce the likelihood and/or impact of potential accidental release. Vanguard Renewables updates the facility prevention programs based on periodic training, process hazard review, incident investigations, audits, procedure revisions, and RMP revisions and updates as required to reflect facility modifications. A notification drill to test the facility's emergency response mechanisms is scheduled for 27 October 2025.

Five-Year Accident History
The facility is new in 2025 and has not had a release of a regulated substance that has caused any injuries to employees or impacted any offsite receptors in the past five years.

Emergency Response Program
As a non-responding facility, the Vanguard Renewables Peterson Biogas Facility is not required to develop or implement an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). An Emergency Action Plan (EAP) has been developed by Vanguard Renewables to provide a formal emergency preparedness program that protects human health and property in the event of an emergency such as medical, security breach, fire, etc. This plan formalizes the arrangements with local police, fire departments, hospitals, and local emergency management personnel in case of an event. Vanguard reviews a copy of this plan with each employee.

Planned Changes
Vanguard Renewables continue
s to review its programs and procedures and make improvements where necessary. Currently, no significant improvement needs have been identified.
